AIRoA releases AIRoA-0 trained on 16,151 hours of handheld demonstrations

Weights and code are available, with 78% average success reported on ten evaluation tasks; the training dataset is planned for later release.

PR TIMES / AIRoA ↗6 November 2026English editorial summary
StoryImages 3Videos 2

Learning from handheld demonstrations

AIRoA released AIRoA-0 on November 6, starting from Physical Intelligence’s π0.5 base weights and using 16,151 hours of YUBI demonstrations. The handheld device records images and gripper trajectories. The reported training uses no robot teleoperation, reinforcement learning or on-robot corrections.

Results within a defined evaluation

Ten tasks were tested 15 times each on Franka at a site outside data collection, averaging 78% success versus at most 27% for four comparison models post-trained on the same data. This is not a universal success rate. Separate operation demonstrations cover Franka, TX-G2, OpenArm and UR.

Released tools and hardware requirements

The model outputs gripper poses rather than robot-specific joint angles; each controller translates them into arm motion, with YUBI fitted. Released resources include weights, data-collection and post-training code, plus inference examples. Sub-four-hour post-training uses one eight-H200 node. Training-data release remains forthcoming.
